The mandatory insurance. Coverage and proof must be arranged before move-in.

It says the tenancy continues month to month if you do not give notice and the landlord does not offer a renewal. That could mean additional rent and ongoing obligations. (§ 12.2)

3. Every rule that could cost you money or get you in trouble
A. Rent and payments

Pay rent on time. Rent is $1,850 per month, due on the first. If it has not been received by the end of the fifth day, you owe a $75 late fee. The fee is charged only once per month and does not increase. (§§ 2.1, 2.3)

Use an accepted payment method. Pay by bank transfer or the resident portal; cash is not accepted. (§ 2.2)

Avoid returned payments. A payment returned by the bank is treated as unpaid and triggers an additional $35 charge. (§ 2.4)

Do not withhold the last month's rent from your deposit. The security deposit cannot be used as rent, even for your final month. (§ 3.4)

Expect rent to remain fixed during the term. The landlord promises not to raise rent during this lease term. (§ 2.5)

B. Security deposit and move-out costs

You can lose some or all of the security deposit through lawful deductions. Permitted reasons listed include unpaid rent, cleaning beyond normal wear and tear, and damage caused by you, your household members or your guests. (§§ 3.2–3.3)

Leave the unit clean and empty. Failing to do so could lead to cleaning charges or other lawful deductions. (§§ 3.2, 12.4)

Return every key and access item. Return all keys, fobs and the parking permit when moving out. The deposit-return clock is tied to moving out and returning all keys. (§§ 3.3, 12.4)

Pet deposits are not necessarily fully refundable. Although the $300 pet deposit is described as refundable, it is subject to the same rules as the security deposit. (§ 6.2)

C. Utilities, insurance and responsibility for damage

Pay electricity, gas and internet bills. These services are your responsibility, and accounts must be established in your name before November 1, 2026. (§ 4.2)

Maintain renter's insurance for the full term. Your policy must include at least $100,000 of personal liability coverage, and you must provide proof before move-in. (§ 10.1)

Do not assume the landlord insures your belongings. The lease expressly says the landlord's insurance does not cover your possessions. (§ 10.2)

Report repair issues promptly. Submit problems through the resident portal within 48 hours of noticing them. If a delay worsens the damage, you may be responsible for the added cost. (§ 8.2)

Use the emergency phone line for emergencies. For flooding, no heat in winter, a gas smell or a lockout, call 555-0142 instead of using the portal. (§ 8.3)

Handle routine upkeep. You must replace light bulbs and smoke-alarm batteries and keep drains clear of grease and hair. Neglect may lead to disputes over damage or maintenance responsibility. (§ 8.4)

Do not assume utility outages are the landlord's financial responsibility. The landlord disclaims responsibility for interruptions caused by utility providers, although it promises to report building-wide outages promptly. (§ 4.3)

D. Occupancy, guests and noise

Use the apartment only as a private residence. It is limited to you and household members listed on your application. Unapproved occupants could breach the lease. (§ 5.1)

Limit guest stays. Guests may stay no more than 14 nights in any six-month period without the landlord's written consent. Get consent before exceeding the limit. (§ 5.2)

Do not run a customer-facing or goods-delivery business from the unit. The restriction applies to a business that brings customers or deliveries of goods for sale to the premises. (§ 5.3)

Observe quiet hours every day, 10 p.m.–7 a.m. Noise must not be audible in neighboring units during those hours. Complaints could lead to a lease dispute. (§ 5.4)

Do not smoke or vape in prohibited areas. Smoking of any kind, including vaping, is banned inside the unit, on balconies and within 25 feet of any building entrance. (§ 5.5)

E. Pets and animal-related liability

Only one qualifying cat or dog is permitted under the stated pet policy. The animal must weigh under 25 pounds, and you must provide its name, breed and vaccination record. (§ 6.1)

Pay the $300 pet deposit before the animal moves in. Do not assume that permission to have a pet eliminates the deposit requirement. (§ 6.2)

Do not keep unauthorized animals. Other animals are prohibited, except fish in a tank of 10 gallons or less and service or assistance animals as required by law. (§ 6.3)

Pay for animal-caused damage and treatment. You are responsible for damage, cleaning or pest treatment caused by the animal. (§ 6.4)

F. Parking and storage

Use only your assigned parking space, number 14. Additional spaces are unavailable under the lease. (§ 7.1)

Keep your vehicle registered and operational. A vehicle that does not run may be towed after seven days' notice, potentially at your expense. (§ 7.2)

Do not store flammable materials in your basement storage locker. Each unit has one locker, but this restriction applies to its use. (§ 7.3)

G. Repairs, access and alterations

Do not make unauthorized changes. Small nails for hanging pictures are allowed, but painting, wallpaper, new locks and fixture changes require written consent. (§ 9.1)

Get written consent and use a licensed installer for satellite dishes and window air-conditioning units. Installing them without meeting these requirements could violate the lease. (§ 9.2)

Expect lawful access for repairs and inspections. The landlord must generally give at least 24 hours' notice, except in emergencies. (§ 8.5)

H. Subletting and ending the lease

Do not sublet or transfer the lease without written consent. This applies to the whole unit or any part of it. (§ 11.1)

Do not offer short-term rentals. Rentals through any platform are prohibited under all circumstances in the lease. (§ 11.2)

Understand the cost of leaving early. The contractual early-termination option requires 60 days' written notice and a $3,700 fee. The lease says this fee replaces any further rent owed after the move-out date. (§ 12.3)

Give notice if you intend to leave at the scheduled end. At least 60 days' written notice is required. Without notice, and if no renewal is offered, the tenancy continues month to month under § 1.3. (§§ 12.1–12.2)

Follow building rules as updated. You agree to follow rules posted in the lobby and resident portal, which the landlord may update with 30 days' notice. (§ 13.1)

I. Notices and changes to the agreement

Send notices to the landlord through an approved channel. Use the resident portal or mail to the management office. Keep a copy and proof of delivery. (§ 13.2)

Check your portal and email regularly. The landlord may send notices to you through the portal, by email or by mail to the premises. (§ 13.2)

Do not rely on verbal promises to change the lease. Changes must be in writing and signed by both parties. (§ 14.2)

Review posted building rules before signing. You agree to follow the rules in the lobby and resident portal, including updates made with 30 days' notice. (§ 13.1)

4. What I would clarify before signing

These are the provisions I'd pay particular attention to as a tenant.

1. The guest limit is unusually restrictive.

Fourteen nights in any six-month period could limit visits from partners, friends or family. Ask how the landlord counts nights and whether exceptions are available. (§ 5.2)

2. The move-out notice deadline is easy to miss.

Put September 1, 2027, on your calendar. Ask the landlord to confirm how notice must be delivered and received. (§ 12.1)

3. Leaving early costs $3,700 under the stated option.

Confirm whether the 60-day period begins when notice is sent or received, how the move-out date is determined, and whether any other charges can apply. (§ 12.3)

4. The building rules can change.

Ask for a copy of all current lobby and portal rules before signing. Clarify whether updates can introduce new fees or materially restrict your use of the apartment. (§ 13.1)

5. Clarify how the deposit will be handled.

Ask for the move-in inspection procedure, how damage is documented, and the process for receiving the itemized deduction list. Photograph the apartment's condition when you move in. (§§ 3.2–3.3)

One final legal caution: this lease does not specify a jurisdiction. Local law may limit security deposits, late fees, pet deposits, entry rules, notice requirements or early-termination charges. In particular, do not assume that a lease provision is legally enforceable simply because it appears in the document.

My overall assessment: The biggest practical risks are the guest restriction, the early-termination fee, the strict notice deadline, your responsibility for worsening repair damage, and the possibility of deductions from your deposit. Before signing, get any important clarifications or concessions in writing and signed by both parties. (§ 14.2)
